brief.meaningEn: A story or experience whose effect builds gradually rather than arriving at once.
brief.meaningZh: 故事或體驗開始時較平靜，隨着發展逐漸累積吸引力或情感效果。
brief.grammar: the film is a slow burn; a rewarding slow burn.
brief.register: Informal but thoughtful evaluation: a filmgoer or reviewer tells another viewer why a quiet story builds slowly and rewards attention; slow burn is not simply boring.
brief.boundaryZh: 須有後來逐漸累積的效果；一直無變化或一開場就高潮都不符合。
brief.misconceptionZh: 不要只因節奏慢就稱讚為慢熱，還要看到後段有回報。
brief.outcomeZh: 能指出故事如何逐步鋪排，以及後段帶來甚麼效果。

sources.file: Idiomatic and Natural English Expressions Books 10 to 16 Part 3.docx
sources.locatorNote: DOCX table 14, row 3; page refers to the locally rendered PDF recorded in the intake summary.
sources.sentence: The novel is a slow burn, but the ending is rewarding.

listening.en: The radio drama begins with small conversations between neighbours. Each episode adds one detail, and the final reveal makes the whole series a slow burn worth following.
listening.zh: 廣播劇起初只是鄰居之間的小對話。每集加入一個細節，最後的揭曉令整個系列慢熱卻值得追聽。
listening.promptZh: 說話者如何評價這部廣播劇？

options.en: Its impact grows through details that build toward the ending.
options.zh: 它透過逐步累積的細節，在結尾產生更強效果。

options.en: Its intriguing opening never develops into a stronger later effect.
options.zh: 開場雖有趣，後續卻沒有發展出更強效果。

options.en: It remains pleasant throughout, with no meaningful final payoff.
options.zh: 它一直輕鬆好看，但結尾沒有帶來有意義的回報。

options.en: Its ending is surprising, but earlier details do not prepare the audience for it.
options.zh: 結尾令人意外，但前面的細節沒有為它鋪墊。

listening.explanationZh: 細節隨劇集逐步累積，到結尾才帶來效果；單有平靜開場或驚喜結尾都不足以構成 slow burn。

reply.promptEn: Why did you recommend the quiet mystery play to your friends?
reply.promptZh: （你為何向朋友推薦那齣開頭平靜的懸疑劇？）

options.en: The clues grow more meaningful in later scenes.
options.zh: 線索在後面的場景漸漸更有意義。

options.en: The ending rewards attention to early details.
options.zh: 結局回應了早期細節，值得細看。

options.en: It is a slow burn that becomes more gripping as it goes.
options.zh: 它是一齣慢熱的劇，越看越吸引。

options.en: The characters change in believable ways.
options.zh: 角色的轉變令人信服。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都合理解釋推薦理由；金句把漸進的吸引力概括為 a slow burn。

scene.promptZh: 一部短片開頭只是記錄老人每天修理腳踏車，片中逐步揭示他免費幫助鄰居的原因，結尾令人感動。哪句最貼切？

options.en: The short film is a slow burn with a moving payoff.
options.zh: 這部短片慢熱鋪排，最後帶來感人的回報。

options.en: The ending is moving, but the earlier repair scenes do not build towards it.
options.zh: 結尾令人感動，但前面的修車場面沒有逐步鋪墊。

options.en: The routine scenes are charming, but the ending adds little to their meaning.
options.zh: 日常場面有趣，但結尾沒有加深它們的意義。

scene.explanationZh: 修車日常逐步揭示免費幫人的原因，結尾讓前面細節產生更深意義，屬慢熱鋪排。

contrast.promptZh: 哪種故事最不適合稱為 a slow burn？

options.en: A novel slowly adds clues before a rewarding final discovery.
options.zh: 小說逐步加入線索，最後有值得期待的發現。

options.en: A film opens with its main twist and stays at the same intensity throughout.
options.zh: 電影一開場便揭示主要轉折，其後強度一直不變。

options.en: A series begins quietly but builds tension across several episodes.
options.zh: 影集開頭平靜，幾集之間逐漸累積張力。

contrast.explanationZh: 開場即有主要轉折且其後不再累積效果，不符合慢熱發展。

dialogue.promptZh: 朋友說：「這套片頭十分平靜，我擔心後面也沒甚麼看頭。」你看過全片，知道線索會逐步匯合。哪個回應最準確？

options.en: It is a slow burn: the clues gather gradually and make the final scene rewarding.
options.zh: 它是慢熱作品：線索逐漸匯合，令最後一幕很值得看。

options.en: A quiet film can still end well, but the middle may not give you much to follow.
options.zh: 平靜的電影仍可有好結局，但中段未必有值得留意的發展。

options.en: The final reveal may be satisfying even if the earlier clues do not build on one another.
options.zh: 即使前面的線索沒有逐步匯合，最後的揭示也可能令人滿意。

dialogue.explanationZh: 朋友擔心平靜開場會一直平淡；金句指出線索在中段逐步累積，結尾才帶來回報。

speaking.en: The story was a slow burn, with each ordinary visit adding meaning to the final reunion.
speaking.zh: 故事慢熱鋪排，每次平凡的探訪都為最後重聚增添意義。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽示範，再說明平凡探訪如何鋪墊結尾。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：學生拍了一部五分鐘短片。前半段只見妹妹每天在空置的店門前留下花；後半段才揭示店主曾照顧她的家人，結尾兩人重逢。用一至兩句英文評價短片的鋪排。
writing.selfCheckZh: 指出前段平靜、細節逐步累積，並說明後段揭曉帶來情感效果；不能只說節奏慢。

examples.en: The student film is a slow burn: the repeated flowers seem ordinary at first, but the later reunion gives them meaning.
examples.zh: 這部學生短片慢熱鋪排：反覆出現的花起初看似平凡，後來的重逢卻讓它們有了意義。

examples.en: It is a slow burn because the quiet scenes build toward the reveal about the shopkeeper and a moving final meeting.
examples.zh: 短片慢熱，因為平靜的場景逐步鋪墊店主往事的揭曉，以及感人的最後重逢。

takeaways.en: The series is a slow burn, but its small clues pay off in the final episode.
takeaways.zh: 影集慢熱，但小線索在最後一集得到回應。

takeaways.en: A slow burn needs more than a slow beginning; its effect should grow.
takeaways.zh: 慢熱作品不能只有緩慢開頭，效果還應逐步增強。

notes: AI-authored first pass; independent editorial and release checks have not occurred.

brief.meaningEn: Feel inclined to do or enjoy something at this moment.
brief.meaningZh: 當下想參與或享受某種活動、食物或內容。
brief.grammar: in the mood for a film; not in the mood for a loud event.
brief.register: Conversational, temporary preference: a friend or cinema-goer tells a companion what kind of film or outing they want now, without claiming it is a permanent taste.
brief.boundaryZh: 表示此刻的興致；不代表以後永遠喜歡或討厭該活動。
brief.misconceptionZh: 不要把「今天不想」改寫成「一向不喜歡」；亦不要忽略對方當下的狀態。
brief.outcomeZh: 能有禮貌地表達暫時偏好，並提出合適替代選擇。

sources.file: Idiomatic and Natural English Expressions Books 10 to 16 Part 3.docx
sources.locatorNote: DOCX table 14, row 5; page refers to the locally rendered PDF recorded in the intake summary.
sources.sentence: I am not in the mood for a serious film tonight.

listening.en: After a noisy day at work, I was not in the mood for a competitive quiz, so I suggested a quiet card game instead.
listening.zh: 忙了一整天，又聽了不少噪音後，我當時沒有興致參加競爭激烈的問答遊戲，便改為提議玩安靜的卡牌遊戲。
listening.promptZh: 說話者為何提議卡牌遊戲？

options.en: It better suited what they felt like doing that evening.
options.zh: 它更符合說話者當晚的興致。

options.en: They had never enjoyed quizzes at any time in their life.
options.zh: 說話者一生中從未喜歡過問答遊戲。

options.en: The quiz had already been cancelled by the organiser.
options.zh: 主辦者已取消問答遊戲。

options.en: They wanted a louder activity after a noisy day.
options.zh: 經過嘈吵的一天後，說話者想要更吵的活動。

listening.explanationZh: 說話者只是當晚較想玩安靜遊戲，不能推斷永久不喜歡問答遊戲。

reply.promptEn: What do you feel like doing after dinner tonight?

options.en: I would like a gentle walk near home.
options.zh: 我想在家附近輕鬆散步。

options.en: A quiet film sounds good to me.
options.zh: 看一齣安靜的電影感覺不錯。

options.en: I am in the mood for a short comedy.
options.zh: 我現在有興致看一齣短喜劇。

options.en: I could sit and listen to music.
options.zh: 我可以坐下來聽音樂。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都直接表達今晚想做的事；金句使用 in the mood for 表達當下興致。

scene.promptZh: 朋友平常喜歡爬山，但今天剛完成長途步行，只想坐在家裏聽歌。哪句最貼切？

options.en: She is not in the mood for another hike today.
options.zh: 她今天沒有興致再去爬山。

options.en: She still enjoys hiking in general and may plan another trip for next weekend.
options.zh: 她一般仍喜歡爬山，也可能安排下星期末再去。

options.en: A shorter hill walk might suit her this evening after she has rested.
options.zh: 她休息後今晚或許適合去山上短走一程。

scene.explanationZh: 她今晚只想在家聽歌，金句準確描述當下沒有爬山興致；一般喜好或另一個較短行程都不是今晚的選擇。

contrast.promptZh: 哪個情況最不適合用 in the mood for 描述當下的興致？

options.en: A person wants a light meal rather than a heavy dinner tonight.
options.zh: 一個人今晚想吃清淡的一餐，而非豐富晚飯。

options.en: A student has always disliked football and is writing a lifelong sports history.
options.zh: 一名學生一向不喜歡足球，正在寫自己的長期運動喜好史。

options.en: Two friends want to watch a comedy rather than a serious drama now.
options.zh: 兩名朋友現在想看喜劇，而不是嚴肅劇情片。

contrast.explanationZh: 一向不喜歡某運動屬長期喜好，並非單純當下的興致；其他兩項都指目前偏好。

dialogue.promptZh: 同伴說：「我知道你平日喜歡恐怖片，但今晚要早睡，還想看嗎？」你今天只想看短喜劇。哪個回答最自然？

options.en: I am not in the mood for horror tonight; could we watch a short comedy instead?
options.zh: 今晚我沒興致看恐怖片；我們可改看短喜劇嗎？

options.en: I usually enjoy horror, but perhaps a short horror film would let me sleep early.
options.zh: 我平日喜歡恐怖片，也許看一齣短的仍能早睡。

options.en: Could we save the horror film and choose a gentle drama tonight?
options.zh: 我們可把恐怖片留待改天，今晚看一齣溫和的劇情片嗎？

dialogue.explanationZh: 金句同時回應今晚沒有恐怖片興致，以及想看短喜劇的具體偏好；另兩句只處理了時間或題材的一部分。

speaking.en: I was in the mood for a simple walk, not a crowded evening market.
speaking.zh: 我當時想輕鬆散步，沒有興致逛擠迫的夜市。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽示範，再說明說話者當時想選哪項活動。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：星期日下午，朋友邀請你去喧鬧的遊戲中心。你剛完成一場長比賽，今天想在家看一齣輕鬆短片，但下次仍願意和朋友去。用一至兩句英文有禮貌地回答。
writing.selfCheckZh: 明確說明只是今天的興致，提出輕鬆短片或其他安靜安排，並保留下次一起去的可能。

examples.en: A trip to a noisy arcade today sounds tiring after the match; I am not in the mood for that. Could we watch a short film at home and visit the arcade next time?
examples.zh: 剛完成比賽，今天去嘈吵的遊戲中心令我覺得疲累，我沒有這個興致。我們可在家看一齣短片，下次再去嗎？

examples.en: After the long match, I am in the mood for a short, quiet film this afternoon, but I would happily join you at the arcade another day.
examples.zh: 長比賽後，今天下午我想看一齣安靜的短片；改天我也很樂意跟你去遊戲中心。

takeaways.en: I am in the mood for soup tonight, though I usually choose noodles.
takeaways.zh: 今晚我想喝湯，雖然平日通常選麵。

takeaways.en: She was not in the mood for a debate after a tiring journey.
takeaways.zh: 旅途疲累後，她當時沒興致辯論。

brief.meaningEn: Attract an audience’s attention or curiosity so they want to engage.
brief.meaningZh: 透過開頭或首個接觸點吸引觀眾、讀者或訪客繼續了解。
brief.grammar: an opening question can pull them in; the first scene pulled them in.
brief.register: Informal figurative audience-engagement phrase: a writer, teacher or film reviewer tells a colleague how an opening draws clearly identified readers, students or viewers into the material.
brief.boundaryZh: 重點是把人吸引進內容的起點；後段能否一直留住他們仍要另看。
brief.misconceptionZh: 不要把它理解成拉人進門，也不要因開頭有資訊就假定能吸引人。
brief.outcomeZh: 能設計具體而相關的開頭，說明它如何引發目標受眾的好奇。

sources.file: Idiomatic and Natural English Expressions Books 10 to 16 Part 3.docx
sources.locatorNote: DOCX table 14, row 7; page refers to the locally rendered PDF recorded in the intake summary.
sources.sentence: The opening scene should pull them in at once.

listening.en: The exhibition welcomed visitors with a mysterious recording of a market call. That opening sound pulled them in before they read a single label.
listening.zh: 展覽一開始就讓訪客聽到神秘的街市叫賣錄音。還未讀展品標籤，這段開場聲音便吸引了他們。
listening.promptZh: 這段開場聲音有甚麼作用？

options.en: It made visitors curious at the start of the exhibition.
options.zh: 它在展覽開始時引起訪客好奇。

options.en: It gave useful background but left visitors with little to wonder about.
options.zh: 它提供實用背景資料，卻少了令人想追問的地方。

options.en: It raised curiosity only after visitors had explored the displays.
options.zh: 它在訪客看完展品後才引起好奇。

options.en: It mainly directed visitors to the schedule rather than the exhibition’s mystery.
options.zh: 它主要指示訪客看日程，而非引起對展覽謎題的興趣。

listening.explanationZh: 神秘錄音在入場之初、閱讀標籤之前引起好奇；金句抓住開場吸引人繼續探索的作用。

reply.promptEn: How could the opening of our local-history video interest new viewers?
reply.promptZh: （我們的本地歷史影片開頭怎樣吸引新觀眾？）

options.en: We could begin with a surprising question about the old street.
options.zh: 我們可以先問一個關於舊街道、令人意外的問題。

options.en: We could show one unexplained photograph and return to it later.
options.zh: 我們可以先展示一張未解釋的照片，稍後再談。

options.en: A vivid first scene could pull them in.
options.zh: 鮮明的第一幕可以吸引他們看下去。

options.en: We could start with a resident’s short memory of the place.
options.zh: 我們可以先放入一段居民對這地方的簡短回憶。

reply.explanationZh: 四個開頭都有可能引發新觀眾的興趣；金句直接說明第一幕能吸引他們投入。

scene.promptZh: 校刊新專題的第一頁先展示一張不尋常的舊校園照片，問讀者「這裏以前是甚麼？」很多人因此翻到下一頁。哪句最貼切？

options.en: The opening question pulled them in.
options.zh: 開頭的問題吸引讀者繼續看。

options.en: The photograph supplies background information but gives readers little reason to ask what happened there.
options.zh: 照片提供背景資料，卻沒有令讀者想追問這裏發生過甚麼。

options.en: The question might interest readers, but it would work better after the whole feature.
options.zh: 這個問題或會引起興趣，但放在整篇專題後面可能較好。

scene.explanationZh: 照片與開場問題令讀者立即想知道答案，並翻到下一頁；其他說法弱化或延後了開場吸引力。

contrast.promptZh: 哪個開頭最不可能 pull them in？目標讀者是想了解社區小店故事的學生。

options.en: Show an old shop sign and ask which store it belonged to.
options.zh: 先展示一張舊招牌，再問它屬於哪間小店。

options.en: Open with a long list of shop registration numbers before explaining any story.
options.zh: 先列出一長串商店登記編號，卻沒有交代任何故事。

options.en: Play a short, intriguing childhood memory from a shop owner.
options.zh: 先播放店主一段有趣的童年回憶。

contrast.explanationZh: 單列登記編號，卻不提供人物或故事線索，較難在開頭引起目標讀者的好奇。

dialogue.promptZh: 朋友說：「我們的自然短片內容很好，可是同學點開後很快關掉。」你有一張動物腳印的清楚照片。哪個建議最能改善開頭？

options.en: Show the footprint first and ask which animal made it; that may pull them in.
options.zh: 先展示腳印，再問它屬於哪種動物；這或可吸引他們看下去。

options.en: Begin by explaining the animal’s habitat in detail, then show the footprint after viewers know the answer.
options.zh: 先詳細介紹動物棲息地，讓觀眾知道答案後才展示腳印。

options.en: Open with a broad overview of local animals before introducing the footprint question later.
options.zh: 先概述本地動物，稍後才提出腳印問題。

dialogue.explanationZh: 同學很快關掉短片；先展示清楚腳印並提問，可立即引發與影片內容相關的好奇，其他安排較晚才用到這個線索。

speaking.en: Viewers saw a strange mark in the sand, and the question beside the first image pulled them in.
speaking.zh: 觀眾看到沙上的奇特痕跡，第一張圖片旁的問題吸引他們繼續看。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽示範，再說明哪個開場安排吸引觀眾。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：學校天文展覽想吸引初次到訪的學生。第一塊展板可以展示一張星空照片，並問「為何這顆星看來一閃一閃？」用一至兩句英文建議開場做法及吸引力。
writing.selfCheckZh: 明確指出初次到訪的學生是 them，並說明照片和具體問題如何在開頭引起好奇。

examples.en: New students could see a night-sky photo on the first panel and read a question about why one star twinkles. That question may pull them in.
examples.zh: 初次到訪的學生可在第一塊展板看到星空照片，並讀到一個關於星星為何閃爍的問題；這或可吸引他們。

examples.en: We should greet new visitors with a clear star image and one question about twinkling that may pull them in.
examples.zh: 我們應先向初次到訪的學生展示清晰的星空圖片，再提出一個有關星星閃爍的問題，以吸引他們。

takeaways.en: For new visitors, a concrete opening question can pull them in before the main explanation begins.
takeaways.zh: 對初次到訪者而言，具體的開場問題能在正式解說前吸引他們。

takeaways.en: Viewers saw the first photograph, which pulled them in, but later sections had to keep their interest.
takeaways.zh: 觀眾看到第一張照片時被吸引，但後面的部分仍須維持他們的興趣。

notes: AI-authored first pass; independent editorial and release checks have not occurred.

brief.meaningEn: Join and leave a group or activity over time without a firm, continuous commitment.
brief.meaningZh: 人在一段時間內自然地加入或離開某個團體或活動，參與沒有固定承諾。
brief.grammar: drift in and out of a club; people drifted in and out of the group.
brief.register: Neutral, often nonjudgmental participation description: a club organiser or teacher tells a colleague that members attend intermittently rather than staying for every session.
brief.boundaryZh: 指一段時間內參與有進有出；不是準時的固定輪班，也不一定是每次同一人反覆出入。
brief.misconceptionZh: 不要把開放式參與錯寫成失職，也不要把單次有計劃的進出稱為 drift。
brief.outcomeZh: 能描述開放式活動的成員變化，並提出相應的安排。

sources.file: Idiomatic and Natural English Expressions Books 10 to 16 Part 3.docx
sources.locatorNote: DOCX table 15, row 4; page refers to the locally rendered PDF recorded in the intake summary.
sources.sentence: People drift in and out of the club throughout the year.

listening.en: The neighbourhood sketch club has no term-long sign-up. People drift in and out of it as their free time changes, so the organiser prepares flexible activities.
listening.zh: 社區素描小組不用報名整個學期。人們隨空閒時間改變而不固定地加入或離開，因此主辦者準備彈性活動。
listening.promptZh: 小組的參與方式有甚麼特點？

options.en: Membership changes informally as people’s availability changes.
options.zh: 成員按空閒時間自然變動，參與並不固定。

options.en: Every member signs a fixed term-long contract.
options.zh: 每名成員都簽了整個學期的固定合約。

options.en: Members usually leave permanently after their first session.
options.zh: 成員通常在第一次參加後便永久離開。

options.en: The organiser changes activities because the room moves each week.
options.zh: 主辦者改動活動，只是因為場地每週搬遷。

listening.explanationZh: 沒有學期制報名，參與者隨時間與空閒程度加入或離開，故活動需有彈性。

reply.promptEn: Why are the Saturday craft sessions designed so newcomers can join easily?
reply.promptZh: （為何星期六手作活動設計得容易讓新人加入？）

options.en: Attendance changes from week to week.
options.zh: 每週的出席者都可能不同。

options.en: Some families can attend only occasionally.
options.zh: 有些家庭只能偶爾出席。

options.en: Because families drift in and out of the Saturday sessions, each craft project can stand alone.
options.zh: 家庭在星期六活動的出席情況不固定，因此每個手作項目都能獨立參與。

options.en: The organiser wants each session to stand alone.
options.zh: 主辦者想讓每節活動都能獨立參與。

reply.explanationZh: 四個回答都支持開放式設計；金句概括全年不固定的成員流動。

scene.promptZh: 社區合唱團允許人們在有空的月份加入，也可因工作暫停，沒有固定一年的出席要求。哪句最貼切？

options.en: Singers drift in and out of the choir over the year.
options.zh: 歌者全年會不固定地加入或離開合唱團。

options.en: Most singers attend regularly but occasionally miss a rehearsal.
options.zh: 大部分歌者定期出席，偶爾缺席一次排練。

options.en: The choir enrols singers at the start of each term and keeps a stable group until the next term.
options.zh: 合唱團每學期初招收歌者，直至下學期成員大致固定。

scene.explanationZh: 有人在有空月份加入、工作忙時暫停，全年參與情況有進有出；另外兩項描述較穩定的出席或學期制。

contrast.promptZh: 以本課「一段時間內不固定地參與」的意思，哪種情況最不適合說 drift in and out of？

options.en: Volunteers join an open garden group when free and pause during exam weeks.
options.zh: 義工有空時加入開放式園藝小組，考試週暫停。

options.en: A technician enters a workshop at exactly nine and leaves at exactly five under a daily roster.
options.zh: 技術員按固定更表每天九時進入工場、五時離開。

options.en: Members sometimes leave a book club for a season and later rejoin.
options.zh: 會員有時離開讀書會一季，之後再加入。

contrast.explanationZh: 按每天固定更表進出，是有計劃的穩定工作安排，不是隨情況自然變動的團體參與。

dialogue.promptZh: 朋友說：「我們的社區棋藝會每月人數都不同，該怎樣準備活動？」這是自由參加的會。哪個回應最實際？

options.en: People may drift in and out of the club, so let us choose games newcomers can join.
options.zh: 人們可能不固定地加入或離開棋藝會，因此我們選些新人容易參加的棋局吧。

options.en: Build each meeting directly on last month’s game so regular players can progress.
options.zh: 讓每次活動直接延續上月棋局，使固定成員不斷進步。

options.en: Set a tournament bracket in advance and leave a few places for visitors.
options.zh: 預先編好賽程表，留幾個名額給偶爾來訪的人。

dialogue.explanationZh: 每月出席者都不同，金句選擇新人可即時加入的棋局；延續上月棋局或固定賽程對流動成員較不方便。

speaking.en: People drifted in and out of the weekend workshop, so each lesson began with a short recap.
speaking.zh: 人們不固定地參加週末工作坊，所以每節課都先簡短重溫。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽示範，再說明工作坊為何每節都要重溫。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：一個免費社區讀書角每逢星期三開放。學生可有空時加入，忙於功課時暫停；負責人希望新來者也跟得上。用一至兩句英文描述參與模式及活動安排。
writing.selfCheckZh: 指出學生不固定地加入或暫停，並建議每次活動可獨立參與或簡短重溫；不能說所有人必定長期固定出席。

examples.en: Students drift in and out of the Wednesday reading group, so each session should include a brief introduction for newcomers.
examples.zh: 學生不固定地加入或離開星期三讀書角，因此每節應為新來者作簡短介紹。

examples.en: Because pupils drift in and out of the group when they get busy with homework, we can choose short texts that stand alone.
examples.zh: 學生忙於做功課時會不固定地參加讀書角，因此我們可選擇能獨立閱讀的短文。

takeaways.en: Visitors drift in and out of the open studio, so the guide repeats the safety note.
takeaways.zh: 訪客不固定地進出開放工作室，因此導師會重複安全提醒。

takeaways.en: People can drift in and out of a club without being unreliable members.
takeaways.zh: 人們可以不固定地參加社團，而不代表他們不可靠。
